Coding agents like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor hand parts of a job to other agents, often several at once. Subagents gives each of those runs one line that reads like a person delegating: the agent, its task in plain words, a live label of what it’s doing (“Reading auth/session.ts”), a timer and how many tools it has used.
Each run’s header is a button with aria-expanded whose name reads the agent, task, live label, tool count and time.

Make the subagent a tool whose execute is an async generator that yields the subagent’s UI messages, so each one arrives as a preliminary output. getSubagentFromPart turns that part into a run, nested tool parts into Tool Calls steps, and the text after the last tool call into the report. Keep the tool on the server and the rendering in a client component.

Parallel runs

Parallel runs share a header that reads “Running 3 agents” with a progress bar, then “3 agents finished in 48s”. Runs can be queued, running, done, failed with a reason and Retry, stopped, or left running in the background. getSubagentFromPart reads an AI SDK tool whose output streams the subagent’s own messages, and the nested steps render with Tool Calls and the report with Markdown.

Runs start folded, so a busy reply stays short. Each line keeps saying what its run is doing, and opening it shows the tool calls streaming into a short window that follows the newest step. When a run finishes, its line turns into a past-tense summary such as “Mapped the token refresh flow · 14 tool uses · 32s”, with the first sentence of its report underneath and the full report inside.
